This batch records the reference facts (arbitrary host Python over CDP, terminal-surface gate, URL literal pre-scan, CDP endpoint precedence, raw CDP method/param guards and the shared private-network boundary), the V2 browser audit (scheme-only navigation, no host floor - D9), and options C1 no port / C2 declarative multi-step plan / C3 read-only CDP allowlist / C4 full browser_exec rejected. facts: browser_exec runs model-written Python on the host through browser-harness over CDP; only output returns; it is gated at tool-definition time by the terminal surface because it runs arbitrary host Python; URL literals in the code are pre-scanned and secrets-in-URL are refused; CDP endpoint precedence: operator BU_CDP_* > /browser connect/BROWSER_CDP_URL/config > hybrid local sidecar > cloud provider > consented real profile > Lightpanda > packaged Chromium; named isolated sessions

browser_cdp exposes raw method/params/target_id/frame_id (OOPIF via Target.attachToTarget flatten); requires an attached supervisor from browser_exec and check_fn requires browser_exec availability + CDP override; a private-network guard refuses cloud metadata/IMDS unconditionally, private pages unless local/hybrid/allow_private_urls, and page-reading methods when the page URL is private or unverifiable; docs state raw CDP must not become a bypass of browser_exec's URL policy

browser_url_policy: ordered floors (metadata/IMDS always refused; private unless local/hybrid/explicit allow; then website allow/deny), DNS participates, JS URL literals pre-scanned because fetch/XHR never updates location.href
reference.adaptation: V2 browser tools are navigate/read/click/fill/dialog in the builtin worker with scheme-only validation and no host/IP floor (verified absent, D9). The contract rejects C4 (arbitrary host Python + full CDP), recommends C1 (no port) and offers C2 (declarative multi-step plan with per-step expected_url CAS and one approval) as the safe way to gain multi-step browsing; C3 (read-only CDP allowlist) requires D9 first plus A coordination for the CDP endpoint/worker protocol

decision_questions: C1 no port (recommended) / C2 declarative browser_plan (<=20 steps, per-step expected_url CAS, one write approval, reuse existing navigate/click/fill/dialog/read implementations) / C3 read-only CDP allowlist (methods whitelist, target verification, D9 floor first, A protocol) / C4 full browser_exec rejected

C3 details: method whitelist, OOPIF target verification, CDP endpoint exposure and worker protocol, platform ownership, mandatory D9 floor, never read/return cookies
